note: Adapted from the original description by Krishna 1956 (English); only the soldier is described, the worker is merely designated a morphotype without a morphological description, so no worker section is set. The measurements are taken from Table 1 of the original (9 soldiers) and transcribed without conversion. Type locality: Sepang, Malaya; the holotype soldier and paratype soldiers were collected by G. H. Corbett on day 14 of month 3, 1930 in the inflorescence of a coconut palm (Cocos nucifera).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head distinctly longer than wide, pear-shaped; fontanelle a circular chitinous opening on the anterior part of the head; labrum nearly triangular, the tip transparent and pointed, with 2 setae; left mandible with a large tooth and 4 small serrations at the base (the 4th the largest), the inner margin of the right mandible smooth; antennae 13—14-segmented; postmentum strongly contracted at the middle; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Compared with other species of Coptotermes, the nearly parallel sides of the postmentum, contracted only at the middle, are the diagnostic feature.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head distinctly longer than wide, pear-shaped; fontanelle opening on the anterior part of the head, a circular chitinous opening, slightly raised around. Labrum nearly triangular, the tip transparent and pointed, with 2 setae. The inner base of the left mandible has a large tooth followed by 4 small serrations, of which the 4th is the largest; the inner margin of the right mandible is smooth, without teeth. Antennae 13—14-segmented. Postmentum strongly contracted at the middle, distinctly wider at both ends. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Measurements (9 soldiers): head length to the lateral base of the mandible 1.13—1.16, maximum head width 0.98—1.01, head height 0.75—0.79, occiput to fontanelle 1.16—1.20, left mandible length 0.65—0.68, postmentum midlength 0.68—0.75, maximum width 0.33—0.38, minimum width 0.18—0.23, pronotum maximum width 0.71—0.75, maximum length 0.38—0.41, midlength 0.36—0.37 mm.
